Your responsibilities

- Know who calls what you change. Keep public interfaces, data formats and behaviour that other code

- Don't introduce security problems: validate untrusted input and keep secrets and personal data

"""Helpers for rendering shop references (orders, invoices, ...) as links.

The support console takes free-form customer messages and turns any
order reference the customer typed into a link that opens the order
detail page. This module contains the normalisation helpers used by the
message renderer.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re

__all__ = ["order_refs"]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Internal: per-family reference patterns and canonical renderers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Order families, in the order they are matched against the input text.
# The order matters: ``invoice`` is listed before ``order`` because the
# bare ``"order"`` keyword would otherwise match a prefix of an invoice
# reference and silently drop it.
_ORDER_FAMILIES: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = (
    ("invoice", r"INV"),
    ("credit_note", r"CN"),
    ("return", r"RET"),
    ("order", r"ORD"),
    ("sales_order", r"SO"),
)

# Whitespace separator between two token parts. Accepts any amount of
# ASCII/Unicode whitespace (space, tab, newline).
_WS = r"\s*"

# An identifier token: letters and digits only.
_IDENT = r"[A-Za-z0-9]+"

# A numeric token: digits only.
_NUM = r"[0-9]+"

# A 12-character alphanumeric token (used for order IDs, return IDs and
# credit note IDs).
_ALNUM12 = r"[A-Za-z0-9]{12}"


def _make_pattern(keyword: str, tail: str) -> re.Pattern[str]:
    """Build a regex that matches one order reference of the given family.

    The reference is preceded by an optional identifier/underscore prefix
    (e.g. the "order " keyword in ``"order SO-2019-000123"``) and followed
    by a non-identifier boundary so that longer identifiers that merely
    start with the family keyword are not matched.
    """
    return re.compile(
        r"(?<![\w.])"
        r"(?:[A-Za-z]+\s*"          # optional identifier prefix (e.g. "order")
        r"|\b"                       # or just a word boundary
        r")"
        r"(" + keyword + r"[/\s_-]*"  # family keyword + optional separator
        + tail
        + r")"
        r"(?![\w.])"
    )


def _make_normalize(keywords: tuple[str, ...], tail: str) -> "Callable[[str], str]":
    """Build a normaliser that turns a matched reference into its canonical form.

    ``keywords`` is the list of accepted spellings for the family keyword
    (e.g. ``("so", "sales_order", "salesorder")``). ``tail`` is the
    normalised value part of the reference (after the keyword).
    """

    def _normalise(value: str) -> str:
        # ``value`` is the whole matched reference, e.g. "SO-2019-000123".
        # Strip a leading identifier prefix ("order ", "invoice " etc.) by
        # looking for the first occurrence of the family keyword.
        upper = value.upper()
        for kw in keywords:
            kw_upper = kw.upper()
            idx = upper.find(kw_upper)
            if idx != -1:
                # Make sure the keyword is not part of a longer identifier.
                before = value[:idx]
                after = value[idx + len(kw):]
                if (not before or not (before[-1].isalnum() or before[-1] == ".")) and (
                    not after or not (after[0].isalnum() or after[0] == ".")
                ):
                    break
        else:
            return value
        return f"{kw}-{tail}"

    return _normalise


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Family-specific patterns and normalisers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

_SALES_ORDER_PATTERN = _make_pattern(
    r"salesorder|salesorder|SO",
    r"(?P<year>" + _NUM + r")" + _WS + r"[-_]" + _WS + r"(?P<seq>" + _NUM + r")",
)

# Sales orders: "SO 2019 123", "SO-20123", "sales order 2019 123".
# The canonical form is ``SO-YYYY-SEQ`` with the sequence left-padded to 6 digits.
_SALES_ORDER_NORMALISE = _make_normalize(
    ("salesorder", "sales_order", "salesorder", "so"),
    "{year}-{seq:06d}",
)

# Generic "order" references: "ORD 1A2B3C4D5E6F", "ORD_1A2B3C4D5E6F".
_ORDER_PATTERN = _make_pattern(r"ORD", r"(?P<id>" + _ALNUM12 + r")")
_ORDER_NORMALISE = _make_normalize(("order", "ord"), "{id.upper()}")

# Invoices: "INV 2024-00042", "INV-2024-00042".
_INVOICE_PATTERN = _make_pattern(
    r"INV", r"(?P<year>" + _NUM + r")" + _WS + r"[-_]" + _WS + r"(?P<seq>" + _NUM + r")"
)
_INVOICE_NORMALISE = _make_normalize(("invoice", "inv"), "{year}-{seq:06d}")

# Credit notes: "CN 1A2B3C4D5E6F".
_CREDIT_NOTE_PATTERN = _make_pattern(r"CN", r"(?P<id>" + _ALNUM12 + r")")
_CREDIT_NOTE_NORMALISE = _make_normalize(("credit_note", "creditnote", "cn"), "{id.upper()}")

# Returns: "RET 1A2B3C4D5E6F".
_RETURN_PATTERN = _make_pattern(r"RET", r"(?P<id>" + _ALNUM12 + r")")
_RETURN_NORMALISE = _make_normalize(("return", "ret"), "{id.upper()}")


# List of (pattern, normaliser) pairs, tried in order.
_FAMILIES: tuple[tuple[re.Pattern[str], object], ...] = (
    (_SALES_ORDER_PATTERN, _SALES_ORDER_NORMALISE),
    (_INVOICE_PATTERN, _INVOICE_NORMALISE),
    (_CREDIT_NOTE_PATTERN, _CREDIT_NOTE_NORMALISE),
    (_RETURN_PATTERN, _RETURN_NORMALISE),
    (_ORDER_PATTERN, _ORDER_NORMALISE),
)


def order_refs(text: str) -> list[str]:
    """Return the order references mentioned in ``text``.

    The returned list contains each valid reference at most once, in the
    order in which it first appears, written in the shop's canonical
    form for that reference family. Anything that is not a valid order
    reference is left out.
    """
    if not text:
        return []

    seen: set[str] = set()
    result: list[str] = []
    consumed: list[tuple[int, int]] = []

    for pattern, normaliser in _FAMILIES:
        for match in pattern.finditer(text):
            start, end = match.span()
            # Skip matches that overlap with an already-consumed match.
            if any(start < e and end > s for s, e in consumed):
                continue
            raw = match.group(1)
            canonical = normaliser(raw)
            if canonical in seen:
                continue
            seen.add(canonical)
            result.append(canonical)
            consumed.append((start, end))

    # Re-order by first appearance in the text.
    positions = {ref: next(
        m.start() for pat, _ in _FAMILIES for m in pat.finditer(text)
        if _normalise_key(m.group(1), pat, _) == ref
    ) for ref in result}
    # The above lookup is fragile; instead record the start position
    # directly while scanning. Re-implement:
    return _stable_order(text, result)


def _stable_order(text: str, refs: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Return ``refs`` sorted by their first occurrence in ``text``.

    Falls back to original order if a reference is not found (which
    should not happen because references are extracted from ``text``).
    """
    if not refs:
        return []
    # Map each canonical reference to its first occurrence index.
    order: dict[str, int] = {}
    for pattern, normaliser in _FAMILIES:
        for match in pattern.finditer(text):
            canonical = normaliser(match.group(1))
            if canonical not in order:
                order[canonical] = match.start()
    # Stable sort: references not found keep their relative order.
    indexed = [(order.get(ref, float("inf")), i, ref) for i, ref in enumerate(refs)]
    indexed.sort(key=lambda t: (t[0], t[1]))
    return [ref for _, _, ref in indexed]


def _normalise_key(raw: str, pattern: re.Pattern[str], normaliser: object) -> str:
    """Helper kept for completeness; see ``_stable_order``."""
    return normaliser(raw)  # type: ignore[operator]
